XSYNC USER MANUALSECTION 7

xs-bench(7) ​

Performance

Measured transfer times against rsync, with the hosts, datasets and evidence behind every number.

SUMMARY ​

Every number on this page comes from a verified benchmark result file in benchmarks/results/, and each table row links to it. Each run is reported separately, together with its hosts, filesystems, dataset sizes and cache policy. Results from different runs are never merged.

The current picture is mixed. Over a 1 Gb/s LAN, uncompressed transfers of medium and large files are limited by the network, and the two tools take about the same time. With -z, xs is faster on the mixed tree in both directions. Several cases are slower today, including a checksum pass over large files pulled to the Raspberry Pi, the single tiny-file pull, and an APFS re-sync with nothing to do. They are tracked as F-07, F-08, F-13 and F-14 in the development status.

READING THE TABLES

Times are medians of verified samples, with the fastest–slowest range underneath. “xs speedup” is rsync’s median divided by xs’s, so values below 1.00× mean xs was slower. CPU is summed across the client and remote process trees; peak memory is the larger of the two endpoints, not their sum.

METHOD ​

The runner alternates tool order between samples and records wall time, CPU and peak resident memory on both ends. After every sample it checks the destination with an independent rsync -anci --delete dry run. A nonzero exit or any verification output fails the run. Setup, deletion of the previous destination, and verification are not timed. A result file is marked complete only after every requested scenario finishes.

ScenarioWhat is timed
fresh-a into an empty destination
fresh-zthe same with -z
noopa re-sync when nothing has changed
checksuma -c re-sync when nothing has changed
tinyone 19-byte file, where fixed startup and handshake costs dominate

Unless a run says otherwise, operating-system caches are left as they are. That is not a cold-cache measurement, and a corpus larger than memory is not necessarily resident either.

HISTORICAL LOCAL BASELINE ​

HISTORICAL

These numbers come from an earlier binary, before the trust fixes and the atomic-write default. They used a different harness (best of three, not a median) on an M1 Max with the 109th Congress slice: 76,838 files, 494 MiB, on one APFS volume. Do not compare them with the runs above.

ScenariorsyncxsSpeedup
local -a, fresh copy15.02 s2.02 s7.4×
local -az, fresh copy15.05 s1.97 s7.6×
local -a, fresh, --no-clone15.02 s6.65 s2.3×
local -a, nothing to do0.77 s0.40 s1.9×
pipe -a, fresh copy19.92 s8.47 s2.4×
pipe -az, fresh copy18.00 s7.77 s2.3×
pipe -az, nothing to do0.99 s0.52 s1.9×

The local rows with clones only apply on the same APFS volume with -a, or at least -pt. Across volumes, or with --no-clone, expect the byte-copy row. “Pipe” runs the real remote code path of both tools through a local pipe (-e tests/fakessh.sh), with no SSH or network in between. The current APFS no-op diagnostic above is much slower than this historical no-op row, on a heavily loaded host with a 98% full volume; quieter, free-volume measurements are still needed.

REPRODUCE ​

Paired SSH run between two hosts, then a summary table
sh
python3 benchmarks/pair.py --runs 3
python3 benchmarks/report.py --run-id RUN_ID --output benchmarks/results/RUN_ID-summary.md
One SSH target through the original harness
sh
python3 bench/bench.py --target user@host:/absolute/root

The full procedure, including fixture preparation, cache-reset requirements and the SSH stream probe, is in benchmarks/README.md ↗. After adding a run to benchmarks/results/, run npm run docs:refresh in sites/xsync; the new run appears on this page without hand edits.

NOT YET MEASURED ​

  • Cold-cache runs on either host.
  • The full 10.53 GB Congress corpus in both directions (the push above is still in progress), and the 1% update fixture.
  • Local copies on Linux filesystems such as ext4 and XFS, where a parallel receiver should matter more than on APFS.
  • A regression gate that fails CI when a scenario loses ground (backlog F-02).
